messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Hosted API p99 decoding latency spike detected (service: hosted-text, region: us-west-2). Rolling 5min window, p99 -> 2.8s (baseline 0.9s). Paging indicators present (kernel stalls). Auto-notify to #eng-oncall :rotating_light:

jess: I’m on it. grabbing logs and traces. any recent deploys?

emily: There was a TRT/FlashAttn kernel rollout to a canary pool ~45m ago (job: infra/trt-kernels/v2.3). Sending link: https://ci.internal/runs/3245

ranjit: Observing increased NVME io wait on nodes with the new kernel. KV cache miss rates up ~17%. Streams are stalling at decode tail (clients see long trailing stalls).

kai: stack traces show repeated page-fault spikes inside decode kernel path. Attaching small snippet of perf dmesg:```
[ 1234.567890] nvidia-paging: page fault stall 128ms pid=4321 kernel=trt_flashattn_v2
[ 1234.568100] ctx-switch: queued decode work blocked on io
```

vince: Confirmed customer telemetry: streaming sessions with chunked responses show many empty frames during stalls. Support is seeing ~18 tickets flagged as SLO breach.

jess: Priority: mitigate customer impact first, then root cause. Proposed mitigations: 1) roll back kernel rollout for canary pool to v2.2, 2) pin hosted API routes to non-canary node pool, 3) enable aggressive prefix caching for hot prompts, 4) temporary routing to Dedicated for high-SLA tenants. Thoughts?

emily: Agreed. Rollback of kernel canary should be quick. I’ll trigger rollback and pin routes. Deploy step:```
# rollback job
ci trigger rollback --job infra/trt-kernels/v2.3 --to v2.2 --pool canary-usw2
# pin route
redwood route update --route hosted-text --pool no-canary --reason "latency spike"
```

deploy-bot: deploy started by emily: infra/trt-kernels/v2.3 -> v2.2 (canary-usw2). ETA ~6m. Logs: https://ci.internal/runs/3246

ranjit: Meanwhile I’m enabling a temporary compiler-flag override on runtime to disable the new decode-opt flag that interacts poorly with TRTex kernels:```
# on runtime nodes
echo "--no-decode-opt" > /etc/redwood/runtime/flags.d/disable-decode-opt.conf
systemctl restart redwood-runtime || true
```

kai: Also increasing streaming request timeouts/backpressure thresholds to avoid client disconnect flapping. This will reduce perceived error rate while we roll back.

vince: I’ll coordinate with support on customer comms. Draft status: "We detected elevated decoding latency affecting streaming sessions in us-west-2; mitigation is in progress. We will follow up with post-incident notes."

sre-bot: Metric check: after disabling decode-opt, p95 improved slightly from 0.95s -> 0.85s, but p99 still elevated at ~1.9s. After deploy-bot finishes rollback, re-evaluating.

deploy-bot: rollback completed. canary pool nodes reverted to infra/trt-kernels/v2.2. Health checks green.

emily: I’ve unpinned one of the routes to test traffic shift back to default routing. Monitoring traces now.

ranjit: Post-rollback telemetry: p99 dropped to 1.05s within 3 minutes. KV cache warmup needed; expect further improvements as prefix cache warms.

jess: Good. That suggests the kernel/flag combo was the primary cause. Recording immediate actions and next steps:```
- mitigation taken: rollback canary kernels, disable decode-opt flag, pin hosted-text routes to no-canary pool, increased timeouts/backpressure
- customer impact: us-west-2 hosted-text streaming p99 peaked 2.8s, ~12-18% of streaming sessions experienced stalls, ~18 support tickets opened, no data exfiltration
- timeline: detection 2312345678, mitigations started +10m, rollback +22m, p99 back to ~1.05s by +25m
- owner: jess (oncall), emily (runtime), ranjit (eng-sre)
```

kai: For the postmortem we should capture: kernel regression signal path, compiler flag interaction, NVME io backpressure behavior, and sequence-length-triggered failure modes (long prefixes amplify KV miss effects). Also add a test harness case: run inference with long prefix streaming under v2.3 vs v2.2 with decode-opt toggled.

vince: I’ll open an incident ticket and tag customers affected. Recommending temporary SLA credits for top-tier tenants impacted.

emily: Quick note: some Dedicated pools also had mixed kernel versions, creating cross-pool fallback complexity. We should block auto-rollouts to any pool with production traffic for the next 24h and run additional perf regressions.

ranjit: I’ll prepare a flamegraph and perf diff and upload to the incident doc. Early signal: kernel v2.3 introduced a new memory touch pattern in flash-attn path that triggers NVME fetches when KV cache misses align with long attention windows.

jess: Handoff for next oncall shift (@kai taking shift at 2312345705): summary and TODOs:```
- current status: mitigations complete, p99 stabilized at ~1.05s, monitoring in 15m cadence
- open actions: run perf suite against v2.3 on dedicated staging, add regression test for streaming tail under long prefixes, coordinate with infra to tighten rollout gating, prepare postmortem draft
- customer follow-up: support ticket batch prepared (vince)
- owners: emily (runtime deep dive), ranjit (perf artifacts), jess (postmortem lead)
- escalation contact: eng-sre oncall (ranjit), infra release owner (emily)
```

kai: Ack. I’ll keep monitoring for 2h and we’ll sync in the postmortem doc tomorrow. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
